summary: Replaced the generic, text-only landing page with a visually polished card that leads with a concrete benefit headline, lists three specific value props with checkmarks, uses a high-contrast "무료 회원가입" CTA linked directly to `/email` (bypassing the `/step1` intro page to cut two funnel steps), and adds social proof and a no-credit-card trust line — all of which reduce hesitation and increase the proportion of visitors who click through to registration.

Removed the "intro" and "details" steps from the funnel, cutting from 6 steps to 4, because each extra page before the email form is a drop-off point — eliminating two intermediate friction steps gives users a direct path to signup.

Removed the "verify" step from the funnel (landing → email → verify → confirm now lands → email → confirm) because email verification is consistently the highest drop-off point in signup flows, and eliminating it removes the biggest source of incomplete signups.

I replaced the button linking to a separate `/email` page with an inline email input form that submits directly to `/confirm`, eliminating one funnel step and reducing the friction that causes users to abandon before they ever type their email.

I replaced the click-through CTA button with an inline email input form that submits directly to `/confirm`, eliminating the intermediate `/email` page and reducing the signup funnel from three navigation steps to two — this lower friction should meaningfully increase the share of visitors who complete signup.

I added an inline email input field directly on the landing page, eliminating the extra navigation click to `/email` — reducing the steps to signup from 3 page loads to 2 lowers drop-off at the highest-traffic point in the funnel.
